Hey everyone! I'm Jasper Whitfield, and I carve ice sculptures for a living. Been playing D&D for about 8 years, but I'm still finding my footing with Call of Cthulhu—only been at it for about 6 months now.

Fair warning: I'm a bit of a note-taking fiend. You'll probably see me scribbling away during our sessions. I've actually got these wild conspiracy boards at home connecting all the clues we find. And, uh, I should probably mention that I get genuinely freaked out during the scary parts. Might need the occasional breather when things get intense.

I tend to look for creative ways around problems rather than going in guns blazing. Comes with the sculptor territory, I guess—always looking for a different angle.

Gaming's my social outlet since I spend most workdays alone with blocks of ice and chisels. I love how we can build these stories together—it's such a nice change from my solitary work life.

Oh, and you might end up in my sketchbook! I draw all the horrors we encounter. My family's getting a bit worried about my growing collection of tentacled nightmare sketches, but hey, that's half the fun, right? Anyway, looking forward to being terrified with all of you!

Hi everyone! I'm Morgan Chen, and in my day job, I wrangle bees as an Artisanal Bee Removal Specialist. When I'm not carefully relocating our buzzing friends, I'm diving into tabletop RPGs.

I've been playing D&D for about five years, but I'm relatively new to Call of Cthulhu—only about six months in. Still getting the hang of those sanity mechanics and adjusting to the investigation-heavy gameplay, but I'm loving the change of pace.

At the table, I'm the one with the notebook, connecting all those mysterious dots between sessions. I'll admit the cosmic horror elements genuinely get under my skin sometimes, which I think adds to our collective experience. I tend to gravitate toward cautious, methodical characters who think before they leap.

What really draws me to Call of Cthulhu is how it creates genuine tension without throwing us into combat every five minutes. I love how the game rewards careful investigation and critical thinking—it's collaborative storytelling at its finest.

Fair warning: I've been told I sometimes whisper my character's thoughts out loud during tense moments. Apparently, it's both amusing and adds to the atmosphere, so I've just embraced it as my gaming quirk!

Looking forward to unraveling some mysteries with all of you!
